newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse seen stabilising next week.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse seen stabilising next week.

text.p: Polish shares are seen stabilising next week on the back of the equilibrium that was reached after this week's 3.8-percent rise to 16,263.8 points.
The market fell 6.1 percent in the previous week.
Analysts said investors needed to employ selective buying as the overall market looked fairly valued at current levels.

"The market should stabilise next week because the WIG fell a lot from the beginning of March and no more deep falls can be expected, and the market could stay between 16,000 and 16,500," said Artur Kobos, a trader at ING Baring Securities in Warsaw.
Some analysts said shares could receive a boost next week if the monthly inflation figure for March due on Tuesday comes in below one percent.

Analysts said a good sign was central bank head Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz's Friday statement in London that the government should achieve its 13 percent inflation goal for 1997 and that the rate might drop to single digits in 1998.
Some analysts said her prognoses might prove too optimistic but at least March's figure could provide shares some mileage.
"I think a number below one percent could enliven the market," said Bogdan Duszek, an analyst at PKO BP brokerage.

But analysts said possible short-term negative signals included 1997's heavy primary market offer, beginning next week with paper firm Celuloza Swiecie's public offering of at least 112.5 million zlotys, which may draw cash from listed stocks.
Analysts also said Warsaw shares could suffer if Friday's U.S. PPI and retail sales data hit western bourses.
They also said some of next week's selective buying would be based on stock picking before firms release March financial data late in the week.
Analysts said the main market's top gainer this week, Kable, rose 20.3 percent after 50-percent owner NKT Kables called a public tender offer at 41 zlotys per share.

Agros, which announced on Thursday its issue of 2,425,000 shares at 70 zlotys each was oversubscribed, rose 16.7 percent, and Mostostal Export rose 16.6 percent, helped by news of a dividend from a subsidiary.
Trade in Espebepe, which rose 5.9 percent on the week, will be suspended on Monday as the firm's creditors meet to discuss a possible write-off of its 75-million-zloty debt.
